issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnMilk() returning a String (UML and instructions), and the template's Main calls messageOnMilk() with no parameters. The solution repository, however, defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implementations in Goat/Seal use this signature). This parameter mismatch prevents students from implementing or using the interface as described and makes the provided example Main code incompatible with the solution signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface signature consistent with the problem statement and template by changing messageOnMilk(double volume) to messageOnMilk() returning String, and update Seal and Goat implementations accordingly to return the format described ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively, if a volume parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to declare and call messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the expected output including the volume.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template Main invoke a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters and expect a return like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked", but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implementations include the volume in the returned string). This is an API/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) and will confuse students: the template and problem describe a no-argument method while the solution uses a double parameter, so students cannot reliably map the specification to the provided implementation or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Milkable API across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update Seal and Goat to return "[AnimalType] [name] is milked" (matching the problem and template), or (B) update the problem statement and template usage to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the volume in the expected return string. Prefer option A to match the original specification in the problem description.
